I don’t have real‑time data in this chat, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the current AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. It provides a live AQI, forecast, and historical data. |
| **Weather apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your phone’s native weather app) now include an AQI widget. |
| **Local news** | Local TV or radio stations often report on air quality during major smog events. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also try a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They usually pull from one of the above services.

Let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what typical AQI values mean for health or how to interpret the numbers!
